top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a quantitative 2011 prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle, since reproduced by many groups and extended across moire systems. A citation worded around flat bands and correlated phases, not the unresolved pairing mechanism, rests on established facts, and the three-name allocation maps onto prediction (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero). The maturity and credit concerns (field under a decade old, Cao and first-author team outside the names) are real, so P003, the mature and cleanly attributed Katori-Ye lattice clock, is my second choice. P002 ranks third because pairing IceCube with the clock rests on a single-name credit for a collaboration-scale discovery without an agreed principle. No award is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as a theorist in magnetism and correlated electrons I have field proximity to the moire and correlated-matter proposal, but no documented personal or institutional connection to the proposed laureates
